title: How to organize the shoe and boot zone | Entryway
description:
Hold the footwear that comes off at the door, and keep the grit it carried in off every other floor in the house.

This is the Shoe and Boot Zone in the Entryway. About 30-45 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Two pairs per person on the rack, soles down, boots standing in the tray, one pair of slippers each, and a clear stretch of floor a full stride wide between the door and the rack.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Pull every shoe out and pair them up on the floor.
Straighten: Daily pairs on the rack at a height you can reach standing up, boots in the tray because they will always come
Shine: Take the boot tray outside and hose it.
Safety: Wet soles on a hard floor are how people go down in this room.
Standardize: Give each person their own named shelf on the rack, the name written at the shelf edge, so a third pair has vi
Sustain: Shoes come off just inside the door and go onto the rack before the coat comes off, while your hands are still

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Two pairs per person at the door, soles down, everything else lives somewhere that is not the entryway.

Full written steps for this zone, free:
https://6s-success.com/zones/entryway-the-shoes-and-boots.html

6S Success turns Lean's six-S method into something you can actually do in a house: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain. One small zone at a time, finished in one session, and it stays finished.
